content:
Reddit announced two upcoming changes that some long-time users may not be happy about.

The company has already imposed one restriction on old Reddit and is now announcing a second. Additionally, RSS support will also be discontinued…

Old Reddit

Reddit significantly changed its user interface back in 2018, which sparked strong pushback from those who preferred the older version. In response, the platform said it would continue to provide access to what it later called "old Reddit" as long as people were still using it.

The first change to this policy was implemented in August this year, when the company required old Reddit users to log in. The company is now announcing that the original interface will be limited to users who have used it within the past six months, and new users will not be able to access it.

Reddit says both measures are intended to reduce AI scraping of the site (although, if you pay, this apparently isn't a problem).

RSS Feed Service Termination

The shutdown of RSS feed is being cited for the same reason.

For subs that use RSS feeds to assist with moderation, this change could be a particular big one. Reddit says it's aware of this and is suggesting moderators use Devvit apps such as Discord Relay.

User Reactions Are Lukewarm

Looking at the posts in the comments section, it's clear that many long-time users are unhappy with the recent developments.

What do you think about the recent changes? Feel free to share in the comments.
